alignments.note: The ASV clefts the fronted prepositional phrase: *It is for chastening that ye endure*. The cleft frame *It is … that* is supplied around the preposition's own *for*, so under rule 67 it rides undivided with the token that would carry the plain case preposition, discontinuously under rule 15, and heads on the prepositional word as rule 78 has it. Materially different alternative: marking *It is* and *that* `added` under rules 5 and 86, on the ground that no Greek token carries the cleft's subordination; I take the frame reading because the fronted `εἰς` phrase is precisely what licenses the cleft, so rule 67's *no token licenses the frame at all* is not the case here. The verse note's alternative rendering *Endure unto chastening* is not the ASV text and is not aligned.
`παιδείαν` → *chastening*; the case preposition has already gone with the frame on `εἰς`.
Inflected verb takes its supplied English subject under rules 7 and 9; head on the lexical verb *endure*, not on *ye*.
Comparative adverb `ὡς` → *as*. No answering `καί` stands here, so rules 82 and 100 are not in question.
Anarthrous dative `υἱοῖς` → *with sons*. No article stands to anchor a determiner, so the case preposition stays with the noun under rules 21 and 36, headed on the noun.

Dative `ὑμῖν` → *with you*. The *with* realizes the dative case rather than making *dealeth* phrasal; rule 36 forbids splitting it off onto the verb, and no Greek preposition is expressed for it to answer to.
`προσφέρεται` → *dealeth*; its object and the case preposition belong to `ὑμῖν`.
Article before the name-like `θεός`, which the ASV writes bare as *God* with no determiner: rule 23. Rules 51 and 60 do not apply, the ASV supplying no indefinite or demonstrative here.
`θεός` → *God*, the subject the ASV fronts ahead of its verb.
Interrogative adjective `τίς` → *what*, modifying the expressed noun; no *manner of* frame is supplied, so rule 99 is not in question.

`γάρ` → *for*. SBLGNT.HEB.12.7.v002 is underdetermined and the projection carries r00-base, which the English permits; no fallback-excluded mark stands, so rule 97 is not this case and rule 12 forbids reopening it.

The Greek clause `τίς γὰρ υἱὸς ὃν …` is verbless and the ASV supplies the existential *is there*. Nothing else in the clause is left to carry it — the relative clause has its own verb — so it rides with the noun under the rule 53/68 chain, headed on the noun and not on the supplied copula.
Relative pronoun `ὅν` → *whom*; no supplied antecedent or generic noun accompanies it, so rule 77 does not arise.
Ordinary negative `οὐ` → *not*, postposed by the ASV's clause order. No negative indefinite stands with it, so rules 41 and 59 are not in question, and it is not paired with `μή`.
`παιδεύει` → *chasteneth*, the same root the verse's `παιδείαν` renders *chastening*.

Anarthrous `πατήρ` with the ASV's italicized *his*: rule 51's anarthrous clause makes the supplied determiner an ordinary rule 7 helper on the word it determines, and rule 11 keeps the italics from making it `added`. No article stands here for rule 20 to empty.

review_notes: All 16 source ids and all 24 target ids are partitioned exactly once.
The only materially contested unit is s001: the cleft frame *It is … that* on `εἰς` (rule 67) versus marking those words `added` (rules 5, 86). Recorded in that unit's note.
No `noncompositional` unit was needed; no preposition-plus-governed-word pair here is rendered by a single English word (rule 94).
Only one article stands in the verse (s008), and the ASV supplies no determiner, pronoun, relativizer or address word for it.
